gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-coptic: Nippo's small letters stand almost capital-tall, drawn in rope-thin line. Noto Sans Coptic fills its lines with open, uncrowded mouths and a dominant middle zone, a sturdy companion beside that taut wire.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-cuneiform: Nippo draws every letter as a single wire-like line, with small letters standing proud. Noto Sans Cuneiform has swollen, bead-like lowercase and an open e; one is made for display punch, the other for reading.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-duployan: Contemporary and technical, Nippo draws its letters with zero stroke modulation. Noto Sans Duployan carries paragraphs easily, its wide-mouthed a and oversized counters letting text run along without snagging on tight spots.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-elymaic: Noto Sans Elymaic reads easily, with apertures open from start to finish. Nippo's wire-cut letters have no hairlines anywhere, giving headings a technical snap while the sans below keeps low ascenders and quietly does the reading.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-ethiopic: Modern and technical, Nippo draws every line with no swing in stroke weight. What stands out is the wiry-versus-sturdy tension: Noto Sans Ethiopic's tall, solid lowercase grounds Nippo's wire-thin lines.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-gothic: Noto Sans Gothic opens its lowercase into big, glassy counters. Nippo is built to grab attention in wire-thin, same-width strokes, while the sans-serif text face is built to be read.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-grantha: Nippo's wire-cut curves keep their weight right through the shoulders. Noto Sans Grantha reads smoothly with tall, open letters, though if Nippo is made small its fine line may fade.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-gunjala-gondi: Bent-wire roundness, standing almost capital-tall: that is Nippo up top. Noto Sans Gunjala Gondi follows with chunky, crayon-tall strokes and wide terminal gaps, a sturdy counterweight to all that wire.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-gurmukhi: Small letters stand nearly capital-sized in Nippo, cut like wire. Noto Sans Gurmukhi, with outward-pointing terminals and low ascenders, supplies the quiet text while Nippo supplies the technical edge.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-hanunoo: Nippo is all wire-gauge strokes, with small letters standing proud. It earns its keep big and brief, while Noto Sans Hanunoo fills most of the line height with open terminals for easy reading.
